findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to name="trigger.expect", unlike FlowRunStateTriggerFields and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields, which use trigger.after when posture is Proactive ("Stays in"), a contract also encoded in flow-run-state-trigger-fields.stories.tsx (after for Proactive, expect for Reactive). A backend Proactive EventTrigger fires on the absence of its expect events, so selecting Proactive + Paused here creates a trigger that fires when the pool does not pause, the opposite of the UI label. Fix by binding the field name from posture like the sibling components.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-pool automation fires when the selected status event is absent instead of when the pool stays in that status.
findings.title: WorkPool status always writes trigger.expect, ignoring Proactive posture

findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to name="trigger.expect", unlike FlowRunStateTriggerFields and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields, which use trigger.after when posture is Proactive ("Stays in"), a contract also encoded in flow-run-state-trigger-fields.stories.tsx. A backend Proactive EventTrigger fires on the absence of its expect events, so selecting Proactive + Not Ready creates a trigger that fires when the queue does not become not-ready, the opposite of the UI label. Fix by binding the field name from posture like the sibling components.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-queue automation fires when the selected status event is absent instead of when the queue stays in that status.

findings.description: This threshold handler uses parseInt(e.target.value) while every sibling (FlowRun, Deployment, WorkQueue, Custom, and this file's own within field) uses Number(...). Verified with node: parseInt("1e2") is 1 where Number("1e2") is 100, and parseInt also silently truncates decimals such as 2.5 to 2 instead of storing the entered value for schema validation. Fix by using Number(e.target.value) like the other threshold fields.
findings.failureMode: A work-pool threshold entered in exponent or decimal form is silently stored as a different number than the user typed.
findings.title: WorkPool threshold uses parseInt instead of Number

findings.description: e.target.value.split("\n") always returns at least one element ("".split("\n") is [""], verified with node), so the lines.length > 0 check is always true and the undefined branch is dead. Clearing the textarea therefore stores expect=[""], and blank or trailing lines also add "" entries, which the zod schema accepts as a string. Fix by filtering out empty lines and passing undefined when none remain.
findings.failureMode: A cleared custom trigger is submitted expecting an empty-string event that never occurs, so the automation never fires instead of matching any event.
findings.title: Custom events textarea can never clear to undefined and stores empty-string events

findings.description: This change flips "strict" from true (base) to false in tsconfig.app.json, violating the AGENTS.md mandate that strict type checking stay enabled with validation via tsc -b --noEmit (the validate:types script in ui-v2/package.json). The diff gives no reason for weakening the app-wide gate that covers all of src. Fix by restoring "strict": true and fixing any type errors it surfaces in the new components.
findings.failureMode: validate:types passes code with strict-null-checks and related type errors that the repository requires it to reject, letting runtime defects through the type gate.
findings.title: tsconfig disables TypeScript strict mode

findings.description: The changed require uses '../email-service/email-event-storage', but git ls-files shows the target was not renamed in this diff and remains 'ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/EmailEventStorage.js'. On a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux CI/production) Node cannot resolve the lower-case path. The fix is to revert this specifier to './EmailEventStorage'-casing (../email-service/EmailEventStorage) or rename the target file in the same PR.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Linux, breaking email analytics startup.
findings.title: EmailEventStorage require points at non-existent kebab-case file

findings.description: The changed require uses '../email-service/email-event-processor', but git ls-files shows the target was not renamed in this diff and remains 'ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/EmailEventProcessor.js'. On a case-sensitive filesystem Node cannot resolve the lower-case path, independently of the EmailEventStorage line above it. The fix is to revert this specifier to '../email-service/EmailEventProcessor' or rename the target file in the same PR.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on Linux even if the storage require is fixed.
findings.title: EmailEventProcessor require points at non-existent kebab-case file

findings.description: The changed require uses '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link', but git ls-files shows the target was not renamed and remains 'ghost/core/core/server/services/lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js'. Verified by checking every changed relative specifier against tracked paths case-sensitively; this was one of three unresolved changed specifiers. The fix is to revert to '../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink' or rename MagicLink.js in the same PR.
findings.failureMode: Loading members-api throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on case-sensitive filesystems, breaking members API startup.
findings.title: MagicLink require points at non-existent kebab-case file

findings.description: Lines 1-4 and 6-10 of the rewritten header drop the trailing semicolons that the base lines had, while lines 12-19 in the same hunk keep them. Repository mandate 19 requires explicit semicolons on all statements, and the Ghost ESLint semi rule enforces this. The fix is to restore ';' at the end of lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10.
findings.failureMode: Lint fails on this file, blocking CI for an otherwise mechanical rename PR.
findings.title: Missing semicolons on rewritten require statements
